currentContext.strengths: Differentiates from firms focused solely on strategy or execution by combining deep technology expertise with an outcome-driven, consulting-led plus technology-enabled delivery model across the full data value chain|Long-standing relationships with 50+ Fortune 500 clients, including deepening engagements over time (one of its earliest clients, a leading global technology company, keeps widening its relationship)|Strategic partnerships with leading cloud platforms, data visualization, engineering and customer data platform providers, including a growing partnership with Databricks, building AI fluency across delivery teams|Centers of Excellence (COEs) and specialized horizontal teams (Data Engineering, Data Science & AI, Data Visualization) deliver domain-tailored, bespoke solutions|First-mover, pure-play positioning as India's first publicly listed analytics company, listed on NSE and BSE since 2021|Inorganic capability expansion via the Decision Point acquisition, adding marquee CPG clients, GenAI readiness and talent pools in Gurgaon and Latin America
currentContext.strategies: Expanding digital solution accelerators and strengthening partnerships with leading cloud and data platforms to capture accelerated AI-led digital transformation spend|Cross-selling and up-selling next-generation analytics/AI tools into the existing Fortune 500 client base as enterprises seek to operationalize GenAI|Expanding footprint in resilient verticals such as Financial Services and scaling presence in European and APAC markets to diversify revenue|Targeted, continued investment to scale Decision Point's RGM/CPG-focused solutions across primary markets in North America and Europe, deepening cross-selling and domain-led AI offerings|Transitioning toward an AI-first service delivery model and establishing stronger footholds in high-value service segments, supported by deliberate investment in human capital (Centers of Excellence, salary competitiveness)|Building a leadership pipeline through the LatentView Leadership Academy (behavioural excellence, people/team leadership, client and growth impact tracks) and the two-year STEP analytics-consulting programme, with intent to scale the Academy into a permanent leadership engine with advanced tracks for senior leaders|Global Innovation Hubs giving clients access to analytics talent to scale digital initiatives, paired with Innovation Labs academic partnerships for early access to emerging talent and research|The Company has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations that sets out parameters for distributing dividends versus retaining profits in the business. For FY26, consistent with that policy, directors did not recommend any dividend and no amount was proposed for transfer to general reserves, with the entire profit proposed to be retained in the Profit and Loss Account to fund the Company's organic and inorganic growth prospects and future business requirements and strategic initiatives. The Company did not buy back any securities during FY26. There are no Associate Companies or Joint Ventures as on March 31, 2026, and no subsidiaries were liquidated, sold, or remained non-operational during the year.
currentContext.expansion: LatentView is an asset-light digital analytics services business with no physical plants; expansion is pursued through delivery-footprint build-out, technology partnerships and selective acquisitions rather than capacity addition. Disclosed initiatives include: an AI Center of Excellence positioned as the innovation engine for advancing AI, Data Science and Data Engineering; expansion of nearshore delivery centers across Canada, Mexico and LATAM, alongside deepening APAC presence through strategic Global Capability Center (GCC) hubs in India, to strengthen client intimacy and delivery agility; expanding footprint across Europe and APAC through pilot programs, proof-of-concept engagements and local subsidiaries; continued evaluation of selective acquisitions in AI, ML and data engineering, building on the Decision Point acquisition which expanded capabilities, client base and geographic reach including talent pools in Gurgaon and Latin America; deepening strategic technology alliances, particularly an expanding partnership with Databricks (plus collaborations with Microsoft and Snowflake) to accelerate cloud-native data engineering; and continued build-out of proprietary IP-led accelerators/platforms (Product Migrate Mate, Data Tray, and ConnectedView for Retail and Hi-tech). During the year the Company also undertook an office renovation with a sustainability-focused design incorporating energy-efficient features and employee well-being upgrades (ergonomic seating, height-adjustable desks, desk exercise bikes, upgraded training facilities).

risks.note: Prolonged economic uncertainty or inflationary pressures in primary markets such as the US and Europe could lead to delayed client decision-making or reduced IT spending.

The analytics industry faces a persistent supply-demand gap for highly skilled data scientists and AI engineers; high attrition or inability to attract top-tier talent could impact project execution and margins.
As a data-centric organization, any breach of cybersecurity or mishandling of client data poses severe reputational, financial, and legal risks.

While actively diversifying, a significant portion of revenue is derived from the Technology sector and top-tier clients; a downturn in this specific sector could adversely affect financial performance.

The digital analytics space is highly competitive, with large IT service providers, boutique analytics firms, and in-house Global Capability Centers (GCCs); rapid technological change requires continuous R&D and upskilling investment, and failure to keep pace threatens market positioning.
Tightening of global data privacy laws (such as GDPR and similar regional frameworks) increases compliance burdens and operational complexities for a data-centric business.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

hero.oneLiner: India's first publicly listed pure-play digital analytics and AI company, partnering with 50+ Fortune 500 enterprises across Technology, Financial Services, CPG/Retail and Industrials.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India's first publicly listed pure-play digital analytics and AI company, partnering with 50+ Fortune 500 enterprises across Technology, Financial Services, CPG/Retail and Industrials.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: LatentView Analytics is a global pure-play digital analytics and AI services company that helps enterprises integrate traditional and digital data to drive digital transformation, offering data engineering, Generative AI-readiness, business analytics and business consulting delivered through Centers of Excellence and horizontal teams spanning Data Engineering, Data Science & AI, and Data Visualization. It serves 94 active clients (FY26) across Technology, Financial Services, CPG & Retail, Industrials, Healthcare and Media & Entertainment, operating from 13 offices across Chennai, Gurugram, Bangalore, the US, Germany, Netherlands, Singapore, Canada and the UK.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- LatentView Analytics Corporation, USA — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary; acquired July 14, 2009
- LatentView Analytics Pte Limited, Singapore — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary
- LatentView Analytics UK Limited, United Kingdom — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary
- LatentView Analytics B.V., Netherlands — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary; acquired April 11, 2017
- LatentView Analytics GmbH, Germany — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary; acquired April 01, 2018
- Decision Point Private Limited, India — subsidiary: Subsidiary (w.e.f. 01/07/2024); leader in AI-led Business Transformation and Revenue Growth Management (RGM) solutions focused on CPG brands; shareholding increased to 80% during FY26
- Decision Point Latam SpA, Chile — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary of Decision Point Private Limited (w.e.f. 01/07/2024)
- Decision Point Analytics Inc, USA — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary of Decision Point Private Limited (w.e.f. 01/07/2024)
- Decision Point Latam, Mexico — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary of Decision Point Private Limited (w.e.f. 01/07/2024)
- Decision Point Analytics L.L.C-FZ, Dubai — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary of Decision Point Private Limited (w.e.f. 01/07/2024)

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: BFSI: $18M revenue (FY26, +80% YoY); CPG/retail: accelerated by Decision Point acquisition (16% of revenue, +18-22% FY27 guidance); Tech: 55% of revenue (down from 70% in FY25), -7M shrinkage from one client but +5-8% FY27 growth expected; Rest of World: 15% revenue (up from 6% 8Qs ago)

guidance.body: revenue growth: 18-20% organic (FY27); margin: sustain 23-24% EBITDA via offshore/nearshore shift & forex tailwinds; order inflow: 18-22% CPG, 40% BFSI, 5-8% tech growth; capex/commissioning: minimal (no major capex planned, focus on talent & partnerships)

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: AI agent platformization via Healtheon (healthcare revenue cycle); Databricks professional services acquisition target; forward-deployed engineer model scaling; global expansion beyond U.S. (Europe traction growing)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Enterprises are increasingly prioritizing data-driven decision-making, accelerated by mainstream adoption of Generative AI, machine learning, and cloud-native data architectures.
- Despite a cautious macroeconomic environment that temporarily subdued discretionary tech spending, organizations continue to invest heavily in data engineering, customer analytics, and supply chain optimization to drive operational efficiencies.
- As businesses stabilize their IT budgets, management anticipates accelerated investments in AI-led digital transformation and expects sustained momentum as clients navigate complex data ecosystems.
- The explosion of GenAI and advanced machine learning models is seen as a significant growth opportunity, with enterprises actively seeking partners to operationalize AI.
- Financial Services vertical delivered exceptional performance, registering 93% year-on-year growth in FY26, seen as a pathway for revenue diversification alongside scaling European and APAC presence.
- Regulatory shifts around data privacy and security (e.g. GDPR-type frameworks) are reshaping industry structure, prompting businesses to seek analytics partners able to deliver secure, compliant, scalable solutions.
- Competitive intensity from large IT service providers, boutique analytics firms and in-house Global Capability Centers (GCCs), plus rapid technological obsolescence, requires continuous R&D and upskilling investment.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: 24.1% Q4 EBITDA supported by forex (+1.1%), labor cost normalization (-1.5% one-off), offset by travel/visa (+1.1%); future margin levers: offshore/nearshore shift for tech clients, sustained USD/INR tailwinds, utilization normalization post-project ramp

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing AI talent hiring, Databricks partnership expansion, potential inorganic acquisition (Databricks-aligned PS firms), Healtheon ecosystem leverage; no dividends or buybacks mentioned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: LatentView is an asset-light digital analytics services business with no physical plants; expansion is pursued through delivery-footprint build-out, technology partnerships and selective acquisitions rather than capacity addition. Disclosed initiatives include: an AI Center of Excellence positioned as the innovation engine for advancing AI, Data Science and Data Engineering; expansion of nearshore delivery centers across Canada, Mexico and LATAM, alongside deepening APAC presence through strategic Global Capability Center (GCC) hubs in India, to strengthen client intimacy and delivery agility; expanding footprint across Europe and APAC through pilot programs, proof-of-concept engagements and local subsidiaries; continued evaluation of selective acquisitions in AI, ML and data engineering, building on the Decision Point acquisition which expanded capabilities, client base and geographic reach including talent pools in Gurgaon and Latin America; deepening strategic technology alliances, particularly an expanding partnership with Databricks (plus collaborations with Microsoft and Snowflake) to accelerate cloud-native data engineering; and continued build-out of proprietary IP-led accelerators/platforms (Product Migrate Mate, Data Tray, and ConnectedView for Retail and Hi-tech). During the year the Company also undertook an office renovation with a sustainability-focused design incorporating energy-efficient features and employee well-being upgrades (ergonomic seating, height-adjustable desks, desk exercise bikes, upgraded training facilities).

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Optimistic and confident; emphasized AI as core growth engine, validated by 49% revenue impact; highlighted Databricks and Healtheon as strategic differentiators; acknowledged tech headwinds but stressed recovery momentum and pipeline strength

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Differentiates from firms focused solely on strategy or execution by combining deep technology expertise with an outcome-driven, consulting-led plus technology-enabled delivery model across the full data value chain
- Long-standing relationships with 50+ Fortune 500 clients, including deepening engagements over time (one of its earliest clients, a leading global technology company, keeps widening its relationship)
- Strategic partnerships with leading cloud platforms, data visualization, engineering and customer data platform providers, including a growing partnership with Databricks, building AI fluency across delivery teams
- Centers of Excellence (COEs) and specialized horizontal teams (Data Engineering, Data Science & AI, Data Visualization) deliver domain-tailored, bespoke solutions
- First-mover, pure-play positioning as India's first publicly listed analytics company, listed on NSE and BSE since 2021
- Inorganic capability expansion via the Decision Point acquisition, adding marquee CPG clients, GenAI readiness and talent pools in Gurgaon and Latin America

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Tech client consolidation risk (one client accounted for $7M loss); AI services arms of OpenAI/Anthropic entering enterprise space; margin compression if USD/INR reverses; execution risk in scaling forward-deployed engineer model

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: AI revenue includes no token pass-through — all revenue retained; Healtheon’s agentic framework is being used as a reusable component for other healthcare clients; Databricks partnership is being leveraged to target acquisition targets with pre-existing Databricks credentials

strategy.body:
- Expanding digital solution accelerators and strengthening partnerships with leading cloud and data platforms to capture accelerated AI-led digital transformation spend
- Cross-selling and up-selling next-generation analytics/AI tools into the existing Fortune 500 client base as enterprises seek to operationalize GenAI
- Expanding footprint in resilient verticals such as Financial Services and scaling presence in European and APAC markets to diversify revenue
- Targeted, continued investment to scale Decision Point's RGM/CPG-focused solutions across primary markets in North America and Europe, …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [New logo wins] Three key clients added this quarter, all described without names: pricing and supply-chain analytics plus data foundational support for "a leading US-based recycled OEM automotive parts provider" (Technology); marketing analytics, dashboard modernization and AI-driven customer analytics for "one of the top asset management firms" (Financial Services); and "Cloud data migration, platform engineering, and data foundational work for a global fintech platform" (Financial Services).
- [Board changes] Two independent-director terms ended during/around the quarter — "Term ended 17/06/26" and "Term ended 22/07/26". The board page lists Anindya Ghose, Dipali Sheth, Mukesh Butani, Raghuama Rao, Reed Cundi and Sudha Sankaran as independent directors, but the extraction lost which two names the term-end dates attach to, so no name is asserted here.
- [Leadership] Sonal Ramrakhiani is listed as Chief Executive Officer, Rajan Bala Venkatesan as CFO, Remadevi Thoathil as CHRO, and Rajan Sethuraman as "Strategic Advisor to CEO"; Venkat Viswanathan is Chairperson and Pramadwathi Jandhyala an Executive Director.
- [Inorganic history] The 2021–Present phase states "Data & AI capabilities scaled through acquisitions", but the deck names no acquired entity, price or date.
- [People certification] "Great Place to Work Certified 2025-26 | 4th Consecutive Year" — the only workforce/ESG-adjacent credential in the deck.
